honda: Two plotted 550 setups: Stage 1.0 and Stage 1.5. Stage 1.5 adds CB300R cams; use matching intake and exhaust hardware.
ktm: One usable COOBER Euro 5b dyno comparison. PowerTRONIC/FuelX reviewed; generic part-throttle claims do not establish a second full-throttle curve.
bmw-r1300gs: Two plotted BT Moto builds: Stage 1 and Stage 2 with velocity stacks. Each has its own stock baseline; Stage 2 fuel labels conflict in publisher text.
bmw-f900gs: Two plotted RS2E setups: OEM exhaust and race exhaust. Wheel PS converted to hp. These are two setups from one tuner.
ducati-desertx-937: One plotted BT Moto Stage 1 setup. BR-Performance catalog targets and exhaust-only charts did not establish a second comparable measured tune result.
honda-africa-twin-1100: BT Moto Stage 1 has separate plotted 91 and 93 AKI tests. These are fuel variants of one kit. 2WDW reviewed without a second verifiable numerical comparison.
suzuki-vstrom-800de: No model-specific measured tuning gain verified. 2WDW/vcyclenut support the engine family, but a GSX-8S test and generic catalog targets are not a V-Strom 800 dyno reading.
yamaha-tenere-700: Two measured tune setups retained: 2WDW with full exhaust and snorkel removal; MotoJP with Arrow exhaust. MotoJP uses a speed axis, so both remain source-only.
ktm-890-adventure-r: Plotted BT Moto Adventure R and Duke runs are separate factory calibrations in one 890 family. They are not two kits for the Adventure. Rottweiler 790 gains are not transferred to the 890.
triumph-tiger-900-rally-pro: No verifiable measured before/after tuning result for the 2020–23 engine. DNK, BR-Performance and Shiftech reviewed; 2024 redesigned-engine figures and catalog targets excluded.
royal-enfield-himalayan-450: No unambiguous full-throttle tune result verified. FuelX advertises part-throttle percentages; PowerTRONIC lists maps. Neither establishes an exact peak gain for this bike. 411 big-bore results excluded.
honda-crf450rl: Two plotted 550 setups: Stock Improved on stock exhaust and Stage 1.0 on a full exhaust, with the same published stock run. Vortex anecdotal estimates excluded.
ktm-350-excf: One numerical 2025 uncorked-build result from Taco Moto. It covers intake, exhaust and fueling together; exact ECU product is unspecified. Vortex/Yoshimura fitment alone is not another verified ECU gain.
ktm-500-excf: Two tuner setups: Taco Moto 2025 numerical test and Pinit 2024 photographed dyno. Different generations, tires and dynos explain why these must not use the 2023 stock run as their baseline.
ktm-690-enduro: Two plotted tuner setups: BT Moto on a 2023 SMC R and Rapid Bike on a 2022 Enduro R with Remus exhaust. Body model and hardware remain explicit.
husqvarna-701-enduro: Two tuner records: plotted BT Moto stock/Stage 1 curves with exact body/year unspecified, and Rottweiler 2017 intake/PCV build with published gain. Neither is a separately measured tune for the 2021 Enduro LR.
suzuki-drz4s: One numerical TST WORX dyno-gain result, tested on DR-Z4SM with RS-12 exhaust. 2WDW and Moore Mafia reviewed without a second verified numerical primary comparison.
suzuki-dr650: ProCycle publishes a 790/725/uncorked-650 dyno comparison. Numeric readings were not reliably retrievable; retained as chart evidence, not a verified numerical gain. Jet-kit fitment claims alone excluded.
kawasaki-klx300: Two measured BDSB setups: ECU with secondary-throttle removal on stock intake/exhaust, then opened intake/exhaust. Peak gains differ from the larger advertised midrange gain.
honda-crf250f: No verified measured tune gain located. Dynojet and EJK fitment products reviewed; stock CRF250F and CRF250R race-bike dynos do not prove aftermarket gains.
honda-cbr650r: No unambiguous numerical primary tune comparison accepted. Moore Mafia, 2WDW, P3 and Carmo reviewed. Carmo legend conflicts with its before/after interpretation; restricted-market derestriction is not a stock full-power gain.
honda-crf300f: No verified measured tune gain located for the 293 cc CRF300F. Dynojet PC6 and EJK products establish fitment, not horsepower gains. CRF300L data are not substituted.
ktm-390-adventure-373: Older 373 cc Duke/Adventure research is grouped in one family. The existing Rottweiler PCV curve and older source-only tune records retain exact tested models and hardware; not the 399 cc Euro 5b engine.
aprilia-tuareg660: Two numerical source records: Throttle Punks ECU/filter gain and Carmo 2026 Rally before/after. Wheel/crank basis is unstated; neither is overlaid on the 2022 wheel curve.
ktm-790: One measured Rottweiler intake gain retained at 6,300 RPM with factory mapping. Power Commander/PowerTRONIC fitment alone does not establish another measured gain.
kawasaki-klr650: No verified measured tune gain located for 2022+ fuel injection. Dynojet PCV and ProCycle fuel controllers reviewed. Carbureted older-generation jet/big-bore results are not substituted.
suzuki-drz400: Two numerical jetting setups retained: JD Jetting/3×3 airbox and SRmoto Dynojet/RS-2. Both are historical SM tests, separate from the 2022 S stock curve.
honda-cb500x: No verified measured tune gain or full stock RPM trace located. 550 and Alt Tune support reviewed; product fitment and catalog claims alone do not provide a measured gain.
